gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Funky Groovy leaves only a narrow slit in its c. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps its curve endings well apart, so pages of running text go down smoothly and never feel crowded.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Groovy draws a friendly, loosely tracked lowercase with a narrow slit where the c almost closes. But Noto Sans Tai Viet opens its curves wide, and that closed-versus-open tension is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri leaves every small round letter generously unclosed, with a high-waisted lowercase. Noto Sans Takri sits quietly opposite Groovy, which earns its keep when big and short.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Noto Sans Tangsa gives its round letters a wide, inviting opening and short ascender stems. And next to Groovy, whose shapes nearly close, a full page of it would feel approachable.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads freely, its counters staying connected to the outside. Groovy holds its curves to a single drawn-thread line, and that gap from the open body is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-thai-loop: Bold-looking lowercase, courtesy of Noto Sans Thai Looped, meets Groovy. Give Groovy plenty of size to show its closed shapes, and let the sans below stay modest with its spacious curve gaps.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-traditional-nu: Approachable Noto Traditional Nushu draws a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, with bowls filling the line. But if Groovy is made small, its narrow slit will likely fill in.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-oxygen: Contemporary Oxygen lets its curves stay open, with lowercase nearly matching the capitals. And Groovy, with its slit-closed shapes and loose tracking, gives that sans-serif body something lively to sit under.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-pathway-extreme: Friendly Groovy spaces its lowercase loosely and nearly closes its round letters. Pathway Extreme does the opposite job, offering clear openings and stubby ascenders beside a big x-height for steady sans-serif text.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear reads easily, its letter mouths gaping like a pried oyster shell. Preahvihear keeps long pages moving with its lofty x-height, a welcome release after the constant-width, marker-like line of Groovy.
